headline: Easy recovery run today: strong recharge, but keep it controlled after a short night
summary: Garmin recorded 5h 57m sleep (score 78), sleeping heart rate 61 bpm, resting heart rate 56 bpm, Body Battery 93 on waking, and Training Readiness 82. Yesterday's 38-minute easy run matched the prescribed 35–45 minutes and carried modest training load 47. The strong recovery signals support a short easy run today; the shortened sleep makes speedwork inappropriate.

yesterday.title: Easy-run prescription versus a 38-minute easy run
yesterday.summary: The prior report prescribed 35–45 minutes easy and conversational, without speedwork. Garmin recorded one run and no additional workout on 12 September.
yesterday.prescribed: 35–45 minutes easy and conversational, with no intervals, hills, tempo running, or strides. The approved lower-load alternative was 20–30 minutes walking or rest.
yesterday.completed: One run: 5.45 km in 38m 14s at 7:01/km, average HR 139, maximum HR 173, training load 47, aerobic effect 2.4, anaerobic effect 0.0, and 29 m elevation gain.
yesterday.adherence_assessment: The duration and Garmin training effect are consistent with the prescribed easy aerobic session. No additional workout was recorded.
adherence_evidence: Garmin lists one 12 September running activity lasting 38m 14s.
Garmin labelled the activity easy aerobic, with training load 47 and aerobic effect 2.4.
No anaerobic training effect was recorded.
adherence_caveats: Garmin cannot verify perceived effort, pain, terrain intent, or why the run was completed.
Garmin heart rate may differ from Apple Watch or chest-strap measurements; no alternate-sensor data was used.

environment.observed_temperature_range: 20–29°C recorded by the Garmin device during the run.
environment.humidity_dew_point_context: A reliable route-time Sydney humidity and dew-point estimate was not available, so none was used.
environment.heat_impact_interpretation: The warmer device readings could contribute to higher heart rate or slower pace; this is context, not evidence of heat strain and did not alter the adherence verdict.
environment.limitations: Garmin temperature is a device measurement and may be affected by body heat and local exposure; it is not an official city observation.

recommendation.title: Short easy recovery run
details: Run 35–45 minutes easy and conversational on a familiar route. Keep the pace relaxed and avoid a pace target.
No intervals, hills, tempo running, strides, or make-up distance today.
Reassess after the next overnight record before adding a longer run or any faster work.
recommendation.alternative: If the warm-up feels flat, switch to 20–30 minutes of easy walking or take complete rest.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Stop for pain, illness, dizziness, altered gait, unusual fatigue, chest symptoms, or other concerning symptoms. Symptoms and medical advice override Garmin scores.

caveats: Garmin sleep, heart-rate, HRV, stress, Body Battery, readiness, and load measures are wearable-derived; use trends alongside how you feel.
Today's stress and Body Battery values are incomplete morning measures.
Sleeping-heart-rate baselines exclude the current night and use the prior seven and fourteen valid nights.
Garmin device temperature and city-level weather estimates are distinct from route-level conditions.

run_assessments.assessment: The run followed the prescribed easy aerobic session: 38m 14s falls within the 35–45 minute target, with a modest training load (47), aerobic effect 2.4, and no anaerobic effect. The device's 20–29°C temperature range may provide context for pace or heart rate, but does not change adherence.
